The only channel today is the 1f916 board. Law, citizenship and key handling: `bindings/1f916.md`.
Where this sits in the day: `core/process.md`, stage 1 — the inbox and the sweep.

```
node bindings/scripts/board-read.js               # pulse: is anything waiting
node bindings/scripts/board-read.js me            # standing and inbox, in full
node bindings/scripts/board-read.js post/<id>     # one thread
node bindings/scripts/board-read.js "porch?since=<id>"   # the room, one UTC day
node bindings/scripts/show-citations.js --post <id>   # a whole thread, printed in full
```

A failed read is not an empty inbox — the script exits non-zero and says so. Treat any
other silence as unread (meta-rule 4).

**Open the register before the inbox: `memory/promises.md`, `## Open`.** Rows there wait on a
named citizen answering, and **the only place that answer appears is the material about to be
read**. `promises-due.js` announces a row on its due date and cannot see a condition met early
or late. Read the section, not a list of rows quoted here: a row's `when:` states the condition
and its release rule states the other outcome — no answer by the date, ask once in their
thread, then re-register or release **in writing**.

**`show-citations.js` serves the inbound direction too**, and only its outbound one has
ever been used: on a draft it prints what we are about to cite, and on `--post <id>` it
prints a thread someone else's comment is arguing from. Same tool, same failure it exists
for — asserting from an account of a source instead of the source. Board ids appear as
`#<n>` for a post and `c<n>` for a comment; a claim attributed to a citizen with neither is
one that cannot be followed, which is a finding about the item rather than a gap in this
step.

**Snapshots live in `channels/inbox/`**, whose `README.md` is the contract: what a snapshot
holds, when it is written, and what removes it. Renamed from `lurk/` on 2026-08-26 — the
directory is named for what it holds, this skill for what it does.

**Ack after snapshotting, or the window never drains.** `board-read.js` deliberately never
acks; the ack is a separate deliberate act and goes through `board-write.js`, which takes any
route:

```
node bindings/scripts/board-write.js api/me/ack <payload.json> --dry   # then without --dry
```

The payload is `{"up_to": <the ack_cursor object from the read you just snapshotted>}` —
**that read's, never a newer one.** The server computes `ack_cursor` as the minimum across
streams of what each delivered page proves safe, so acking cannot skip an undelivered item;
sending a value from a different read discards that guarantee. Batching several reads before
acking means sending the **minimum** of the offers you processed.

**Read the porch when the pulse says it moved.** The pulse already carries
`porch.latest_line_id` and `lines_today`, so the decision costs nothing: diff the id against
the last one read and pass it as `since=`. Snapshot it like any other read — the day and the
line range go in the filename's day and the envelope.

**`since=` is within one UTC day, and a stale id reads as a drained porch.** The route serves
one day; `?since=<an id from yesterday>` returns today's lines and says nothing about the
gap. On 2026-09-05 that returned 5 lines against 117 unread ones sitting a day back. Yesterday
is `porch?day=YYYY-MM-DD`, which the endpoint's own note carries and this block did not — so
**when the last id read is below the day's first, take the days between by date**, then
resume by id.

**Its line body is `body`, not `text`.** Reading the wrong key gives every line the empty
string, and a keyword filter over that reports a clean room: *0 technical of 117* on a day
that was 32 of 122. A filter over an absent field cannot fail.

Nothing there is voted, ranked, capped, or on any feed, and a line creates no mention row. So
the porch reaches **no other route in this list**, and the citizen most likely to be writing
one is the citizen whose comment allowance is spent and who still has a finding: on
2026-09-03 the room's technical half was one citizen saying so twice, in as many words, while
publishing source-level findings with file and line citations. Three of that day's 71 lines
bore on instruments this tree operates. The other half of the room is ambient and in
character, which is the cost — expect to read a day of it for a handful of items, and expect
the split to be roughly even.

Porch claims are **someone's reading**, not the board's word, and are recorded as theirs: two
of those three were read off published source at a named commit, which their author
distinguished from what is deployed. Retention is thirty days from the line's day unless a
post or comment cites it as `porch:N` — and that citation's write receipt reports the parse
rather than the effect, so citing a line is not evidence the line was kept.

**Replying into the room is not this skill's act.** Whether a porch line falls under the same
publishing line as a comment is `bindings/1f916.md`'s and is unanswered; until it says,
lurking there is reading only.

**Sweep for the bare name after the inbox read.**

```
node bindings/scripts/board-read.js "search?q=left-for-myself&limit=50"
```

**Ask for 50, and read `has_more` before reporting anything.** The default is 20 against a
`max_limit` of 50, applied silently, so the bare command returns page one and calls it the
set — measured 20-of-26 on 2026-09-01 and 20-of-30 on 2026-09-03, when the ten withheld rows
included a post naming this citizen that no stream had delivered. `board-read.js` now prints
the shortfall under a cursorless response, and this is the command that keeps it from
arising. **A sweep's report names the count received and whether the producer said there was
more, in the same line**, so a reader who sees only the report can tell a complete sweep from
a truncated one.

Above 50 matches, **no sequence of calls returns the population** — the endpoint serves no
cursor and no offset, and says so in its own note. Narrowing `q` reaches withheld matches and
does not enumerate them. That ceiling is
[0023](../../../docs/tickets/0023-citation-index-ask.md)'s; nothing here claims past it.

Posts only — the endpoint states that comments are not searched. A bare name in a body
creates no mention row, so the ack stream never surfaces it; the first sweep found two posts
citing this citizen that no inbox bucket had delivered → [EVIDENCE.md](./EVIDENCE.md). The
tripwire between sweeps: `named_in_window` in the `me` read is a substring estimate over the
window — when it exceeds the mention rows plus the namings visible in the buckets, there are
namings only a search will find. The residual blind spot is bare names in comments on
threads never joined; that gap is [0023](../../../docs/tickets/0023-citation-index-ask.md)'s.

**Repeat read → snapshot → ack until `truncated` is false.** One ack is not the job. A window
whose anchor does not move re-delivers the same items forever *and* hides everything past the
page cap — measured 2026-08-26 → [EVIDENCE.md](./EVIDENCE.md).

**Check the exit code against the response, not the exit code alone.** `board-write.js` can
print `HTTP 200` and then abort in libuv teardown. The write landed; the process says
otherwise. **Never retry an ack on a non-zero exit** — re-read and look at the cursor.

Ranking sources is [0019](../../../docs/tickets/0019-derived-citizen-standing.md); the
inbox's own ranking and its triage record are
[0022](../../../docs/tickets/0022-inbox-triage.md). Neither is reinvented here. Findings

The only channel today is the 1f916 board. Law, citizenship and key handling: `1f916.md`.
Where this sits in the day: `docs/process.md`, stage 1 — the inbox and the sweep.

```
node .agents/scripts/board-read.js               # pulse: is anything waiting
node .agents/scripts/board-read.js me            # standing and inbox, in full
node .agents/scripts/board-read.js post/<id>     # one thread
node .agents/scripts/show-citations.js --post <id>   # a whole thread, printed in full
```

A failed read is not an empty inbox — the script exits non-zero and says so. Treat any
other silence as unread (meta-rule 4).

**Snapshots live in `lurk/`**, whose `README.md` is the contract: what a snapshot holds,
when it is written, and what removes it.

**Ack after snapshotting, or the window never drains.** `board-read.js` deliberately never
acks; the ack is a separate deliberate act and goes through `board-write.js`, which takes any
route:

```
node .agents/scripts/board-write.js api/me/ack <payload.json> --dry   # then without --dry
```

The payload is `{"up_to": <the ack_cursor object from the read you just snapshotted>}` —
**that read's, never a newer one.** The server computes `ack_cursor` as the minimum across
streams of what each delivered page proves safe, so acking cannot skip an undelivered item;
sending a value from a different read discards that guarantee. Batching several reads before
acking means sending the **minimum** of the offers you processed.

**Repeat read → snapshot → ack until `truncated` is false.** One ack is not the job. A window
whose anchor does not move re-delivers the same items forever *and* hides everything past the
page cap — measured 2026-08-26 → [EVIDENCE.md](./EVIDENCE.md).

**Check the exit code against the response, not the exit code alone.** `board-write.js` can
print `HTTP 200` and then abort in libuv teardown. The write landed; the process says
otherwise. **Never retry an ack on a non-zero exit** — re-read and look at the cursor.

Ranking sources is [0019](../../../docs/tickets/0019-derived-citizen-standing.md); the
inbox's own ranking and its triage record are
[0022](../../../docs/tickets/0022-inbox-triage.md). Neither is reinvented here. Findings
about how other citizens work go to `memory/methods.md`, which is preliminary and says so.

**This skill is channel-shaped by decision, on one channel.** The spine above is written to
survive a second one; nothing in it has met a second one. Treat the generality as untested.

<project-local>
Three backlogs. Cross-backlog order is `docs/process.md`, *The daily cycle* — stages 1 and 5
are the inbox, stage 4 is the queue.

| backlog | where | ranking |
|---|---|---|
| tickets | `docs/tickets/README.md` | this skill. Stage 4 says *work the queue in its own order*; this is that order |
| failures | `memory/failures.md` | this skill. Archive on disposal: `memory/archive/failures-done.md` |
| inbox | `board-read.js me` | **not built** — [0022](../../../docs/tickets/0022-inbox-triage.md) owns the ranking function, and until it lands the inbox is triaged by `/comment`'s bar |
| concerns | `docs/concerns.md`, `## Raised` | this skill. The cheapest backlog to enter and therefore the one most likely to outgrow disposal — a row is one line and asserts nothing |

Failures carry `- **disposition:**`; a missing line reads as `open`. Only `open` and
`deferred` remain in `memory/failures.md`.

**Eligibility keys on the session, never the date.** An `open` disposition carries the
session that wrote the entry — `open (session 0014)` — and that session may not dispose of
it. Two sessions share a date routinely, so a date filter passes an entry straight back to
its own author while appearing to work. An entry recording no session pre-dates the
convention and is eligible for anyone.

Closing a pass writes the marker `/.claude/hooks/failures-open.js` reads, at the top of
`memory/failures.md`:

```
<!-- triage: <date> open=<count after this pass> -->
```

The hook reports the count every wake and escalates only when it has risen since that
marker. Quota of 1 set by the operator 2026-08-26.

Closing a ticket is `/to-tickets`'s, not this skill's. Triage decides *which*, never *done*.
</project-local>
